PF_STEPS|/planF/points/2: the slip class is produced by the finish: {ANTI} in the seal (R10 / R11) or quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm broadcast under the top seal (R11, up to R12)
PF_STEPS|/planF/points/3: joints of the slab are taken through the coating and filled elastic; machine bases and breakouts are grouted before the coating
PF_STEPS|/planF/points/4: a trial area where the substrate is in doubt; the applicable safety data sheets are observed
PF_STEPS|/planF/src: brochure · GBM · SG3 · SG2 · B351 · V360W · V2370
PF_STEPS|/prepF/short: Shot-blasted or ground to an open-pored, grippy surface; laitance, coatings and loose parts removed; vacuumed dust-free; ≥ 1.5 N/mm².
PF_STEPS|/prepF/overview: The substrate must be load-bearing, firm, grippy, dust-free and open-pored: laitance, sinter layers, old coatings, separating agents and loose parts are removed by shot blasting (or grinding, milling) so that the aggregate is exposed and the pores open; the surface is vacuumed dust-free immediately before the primer. The surface tensile strength is at least 1.5 N/mm² (concrete min. C20/25, screed min. CT-C25-F6; plaster P III a/b at least 0.8 N/mm²). The preparation follows DIN EN 14879-1:2005, section 4.2 et seq.; the substrate temperature is 10–35 °C and at least 3 °C above the dew point.
PF_STEPS|/prepF/points/0: shot blasting is the standard preparation for floors: dust-free, uniform, no water into the slab †
PF_STEPS|/prepF/points/1: oil crusts are removed mechanically before the cleaning with {R008}
PF_STEPS|/prepF/points/2: cracks, breakouts and hollow spots are made good before the primer ({K4031}, {EV200}); cracks are closed beforehand, e.g. with {GHS} ({V360})
PF_STEPS|/prepF/points/3: the joints of the slab are cut clean and kept free for {IPU}
PF_STEPS|/prepF/points/4: the primer follows on the day of the preparation so that no new dust and no moisture settle †
PF_STEPS|/moistF/title: Check the residual moisture and the dew point
PF_STEPS|/moistF/short: Residual moisture by the CM method: ≤ 4 CM-% for the resin systems, ≤ 5 for {V360}, ≤ 6 for {V2370}; above that the barrier primers; the substrate at least 3 °C above the dew point.
PF_STEPS|/moistF/overview: The residual moisture of the substrate is measured with the CM device: the resin coatings and seals need ≤ 4 CM-%, {V360} ≤ 5 CM-%, {V2370} ≤ 6 CM-%. A substrate that is matt damp, young, without a vapour barrier or under ground water is primed with the barrier primers {SG3}, {SG3F} or {SG3T} (floor, wall, overhead) — they bond to damp concrete and block vapour and negative pressing water up to 3 bar; oil-contaminated and damp concrete takes {SG2}. The climate is checked throughout the work: substrate and air 10–35 °C (10–30 °C for {V2260} and {V2370}), at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity at most 80 % (65 % for {V360}).
PF_STEPS|/moistF/points/0: no sealed water film on the substrate; damp substrates are matt damp, not wet
PF_STEPS|/moistF/points/1: below the dew point distance the resin blushes and the bond fails: the dew point is measured, not estimated †
PF_STEPS|/moistF/points/2: the barrier primers are not an allowance for standing water: hydrostatic pressure above 3 bar is a waterproofing task
PF_STEPS|/moistF/points/3: the material temperature ideally +15 °C: cold material is viscous, warm material shortens the pot life
PF_STEPS|/moistF/src: SG3 · SG2 · SG3-thix · V360W · V2260 · V2370
PF_STEPS|/cleanF/short: {R008} diluted with tap water, sprayed, scrubbed criss-cross until brownish, left for 10 minutes, scrubbed again, rinsed with hot water and vacuumed — repeated until no oil remains; the surface is not dried off.
PF_STEPS|/cleanF/overview: After the oil crusts have been removed mechanically and the surface has been shot-blasted, the cleaning concentrate {R008} is diluted with tap water as the data sheet prescribes, sprayed onto the surface and scrubbed in criss-cross until the solution turns brownish; it is left for approx. 10 minutes, scrubbed again, rinsed with hot clear water (60–80 °C) and picked up with a wet vacuum. The procedure is repeated until no oil remains. The surface is not dried off: the primer {SG2} (or {SG3T}) must meet the damp, oil-free concrete.
PF_STEPS|/cleanF/points/0: {R008} is solvent-free and phosphate-free; approx. 70–250 ml of concentrate per m² depending on the dilution
PF_STEPS|/cleanF/points/1: the brownish colour of the solution shows the oil going into the emulsion
PF_STEPS|/cleanF/points/2: hot water rinses the emulsion out of the pores; a wet vacuum takes it up — it is not left to dry back in †
PF_STEPS|/cleanF/points/3: the same concentrate cleans the finished floor in service
PF_STEPS|/repairF/short: Breakouts and holes filled with {K4031} or {EV200}; anchors set in {K4031}; cracks closed before the coating; the mortar flush with the slab.
PF_STEPS|/repairF/overview: Breakouts, holes and hollow spots are made good before the primer, so that the coating meets a level, closed substrate: small repairs and anchor holes with the thixotropic epoxy adhesive {K4031} (drill holes at least 6 mm larger than the anchor, cleaned, filled, the anchor set with rotary movements), larger breakouts, gullies and cavities with the flowable epoxy mortar {EV200} in 10–200 mm. Cracks are closed beforehand (e.g. with {GHS}). The repairs are overcoated within their windows — {K4031} after 16–24 hours, {EV200} after 12–72 hours without primer.
PF_STEPS|/repairF/points/0: {K4031}: mixing ratio 2 : 1, pot life approx. 60 minutes, adhesive open time at least 90 minutes; ≥ 2 N/mm² on concrete and steel
PF_STEPS|/repairF/points/1: {EV200}: ≥ 2 N/mm², watertight to 5 bar from 10 mm; approx. 1.9 kg/m² per mm
PF_STEPS|/repairF/points/2: hollow sounding areas are cut out to sound concrete and filled †
PF_STEPS|/repairF/points/3: the surface of the repair is sanded if the overcoat window has passed
PF_STEPS|/primeF/short: {GBM} mixed 100 : 50, rolled into the open pores in one or two steps until the surface is pore-sealed, approx. 0.30–0.50 kg/m² per step; quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm broadcast onto the fresh last coat.
PF_STEPS|/primeF/overview: The component A is stirred, the component B added completely and both mixed for approx. 3 minutes with a slow stirrer (approx. 300 rpm) at an ideal material temperature of +15 °C; the mix is poured into a clean container and stirred again. {GBM} (100 : 50 parts by weight, pot life approx. 35 minutes) is applied with the roller or the rubber squeegee and back-rolled in one or two steps until the surface is pore-sealed — approx. 0.30–0.50 kg/m² per step depending on the absorbency. Quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm is broadcast onto the fresh last coat as the key for the coating; the loose sand is swept and vacuumed after hardening. The coating follows after min. approx. 12 hours and within 24 hours.
PF_STEPS|/primeF/points/0: {G1270} (approx. 130 mPa·s, 100 : 27) is the alternative where the substrate must be impregnated and consolidated
PF_STEPS|/primeF/points/1: keep damp off for approx. 4–6 hours after application
PF_STEPS|/primeF/points/2: foot traffic after approx. 12 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days; approx. 70 N/mm² compressive
PF_STEPS|/primeF/points/3: the primer is also the binder of the scratch coat (1 : 1 with quartz sand) and of the epoxy screeds (3 : 25)
PF_STEPS|/barrierF/title: Apply the barrier primer on damp concrete
PF_STEPS|/barrierF/short: {SG3} mixed 100 : 52 in two coats on the matt damp or young concrete, approx. 0.40–0.70 kg/m² in total; quartz sand 1–1.5 kg/m² on the second coat; watertight to 3 bar.
PF_STEPS|/barrierF/overview: On the matt damp, young or vapour-loaded concrete the solvent-free barrier primer {SG3} is applied in two coats — the first rolled criss-cross into the pores, the second after min. 12 hours and within 5 days, broadcast with quartz sand (approx. 1–1.5 kg/m²) as the key for the coating; approx. 0.40–0.70 kg/m² in total. Mixing 100 : 52 parts by weight for approx. 3 minutes, pot life approx. 35 minutes. The hardened film blocks vapour and negative pressing water up to 3 bar (methane barrier tested) and gives ≥ 1.5 N/mm² on concrete from dry to matt damp.
PF_STEPS|/barrierF/points/0: the non-sanded first coat is walked only with clean overshoes
PF_STEPS|/barrierF/points/1: the second coat sealed with sand carries the coating: {B351}, the scratch coat or the epoxy screed
PF_STEPS|/barrierF/points/2: approx. 58 N/mm² flexural, approx. 76 N/mm² compressive; EMICODE EC 1PLUS
PF_STEPS|/barrierF/points/3: on the plinth, the wall and overhead the thixotropic {SG3T} replaces {SG3}
PF_STEPS|/fastF/short: {SG3F}: the same barrier, overcoated after approx. 3.5 hours — two coats in one shift; pot life approx. 15–20 minutes; the coating within 5 days.
PF_STEPS|/fastF/overview: Where the schedule leaves no night between the coats, {SG3F} replaces {SG3}: mixed 100 : 47 parts by weight, pot life approx. 15–20 minutes, the second coat after approx. 3.5 hours and the coating within approx. 5 days. The barrier is the same — sd > 100 m (class III), watertight to 3 bar, ≥ 1.5 N/mm² on dry to matt damp concrete — and the resin also makes the fast repair mortar and the epoxy screed (3 : 25) that carries load again quickly (approx. 85 N/mm² after curing).
PF_STEPS|/fastF/points/0: small batches: the short pot life is planned with the applicator
PF_STEPS|/fastF/points/1: quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 or 0.5–1.0 mm, approx. 1–1.5 kg/m², on the fresh primer
PF_STEPS|/fastF/points/2: as the joint primer under {IPU}: approx. 200 g/m² absorbent, 150 g/m² non-absorbent, the joint filled after 3.5–48 hours
PF_STEPS|/fastF/points/3: drainage mortar 1 : 25 for the slope under gullies
PF_STEPS|/oilF/title: Prime the oil-contaminated concrete with ASODUR-SG2
PF_STEPS|/oilF/short: {SG2} mixed 100 : 12 on the cleaned, still matt damp concrete, approx. 0.60–1.00 kg/m²; quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm over the whole fresh surface; blocks oil, vapour and water to 3 bar.
PF_STEPS|/oilF/overview: On the concrete cleaned with {R008} and still matt damp the special primer {SG2} is applied: mixed 100 : 12 parts by weight for approx. 3 minutes (pot life approx. 60 minutes), applied with the rubber squeegee and back-rolled, approx. 0.60–1.00 kg/m². It bonds to the damp concrete, displaces the water from the capillaries of the surface and blocks capillary-rising oil and vapour (sd > 100 m, class III) as well as negative water pressure up to 3 bar; it is radon tight. Quartz sand Ø 0.5–1.0 mm is broadcast over the whole fresh surface; the loose sand is removed when cured, and the coating follows after approx. 12–24 hours.
PF_STEPS|/oilF/points/0: the surface is not dried off after the cleaning: {SG2} needs the damp, oil-free concrete
PF_STEPS|/oilF/points/1: approx. 100 N/mm² compressive, approx. 42 N/mm² flexural; ≥ 1.5 N/mm² on dry to matt damp concrete
PF_STEPS|/oilF/points/2: the capillary-breaking mortar: approx. 1 part resin mix : 1 part quartz sand, approx. 2.2 kg/m² per mm
PF_STEPS|/oilF/points/3: where the oil is only on the surface and the concrete dry, {GBM} after the cleaning is sufficient — the trial area decides
PF_STEPS|/thixF/title: Prime plinth, wall and overhead with ASODUR-SG3-thix
PF_STEPS|/thixF/short: {SG3T}, the thixotropic barrier primer, mixed 100 : 26, approx. 0.60–1.00 kg/m², by squeegee, brush, roller or airless spray; sd ≈ 105 m, watertight to 3 bar; the primer under {V2370}.
PF_STEPS|/thixF/overview: The thixotropic paste {SG3T} stays on the plinth, the wall and the ceiling: mixed 100 : 26 parts by weight for approx. 3 minutes (pot life approx. 35 minutes) and applied with the rubber squeegee, brush, roller or airless spray at approx. 0.60–1.00 kg/m². It blocks vapour (sd approx. 105 m) and negative pressing water up to 3 bar, bonds to damp concrete (≥ 1.5 N/mm²), and is the primer of the cementitious substrates under the sealing coating {V2370} — rolled criss-cross on floor and walls of the sewage structure. Overcoat after min. 12 hours, max. 5 days.
PF_STEPS|/thixF/points/0: on oil-contaminated substrates after the pre-treatment with {R008} and warm water (approx. 50–70 °C), not dried off
PF_STEPS|/thixF/points/1: the capillary-breaking mortar: resin mix : quartz sand 1 : 4.17 by weight (e.g. 6 kg + 25 kg)
PF_STEPS|/thixF/points/3: steel that is not coated within 4 hours of cleaning is primed with {SG3T} before {EV200}
PF_STEPS|/scratchF/short: The primer resin mixed 1 : 1 by weight with quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm (2–3 % {FF} on slopes), spread on the fresh primer with the scratch filler method, approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm, sanded while fresh.
PF_STEPS|/scratchF/overview: Rough, pitted or uneven substrates are levelled with a scratch coat before the coating: the primer resin ({GBM}, {G1270} or {SG3}) mixed 1 : 1 by weight with kiln-dried quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.6 mm — with 2–3 % {FF} on vertical and sloping surfaces so that it does not run — spread in one step with the scratch filler method on the fresh or sanded primer and broadcast with quartz sand while fresh. Approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm of thickness; the coating follows after 12–24 hours.
PF_STEPS|/scratchF/points/0: thicker levelling (5–30 mm mortar, 11–150 mm screed) with the epoxy screed 3 : 25 — resin : quartz sand Ø 0.06–3.5 mm
PF_STEPS|/scratchF/points/1: with {V360} the levelling is made with the seal itself: 1 : 0.5 with quartz sand Ø 0.1–0.35 mm up to 2 mm, pinholes with approx. 3 % {FF}
PF_STEPS|/scratchF/points/2: a sanded scratch coat is swept and vacuumed before the coating
PF_STEPS|/scratchF/points/3: where the slab is level and closed the scratch coat is omitted
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/title: Grout machine bases and breakouts with ASODUR-EV200
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/short: {EV200}, the flowable three-component epoxy mortar, 10–200 mm in one skin, self-compacting, without primer; approx. 65 N/mm² after 24 hours, 109 N/mm² after 7 days; approx. 1.9 kg/m² per mm.
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/overview: Machine bases, crane rails, railing and support posts, anchors, gullies, cavities and breakouts are grouted with {EV200}: the components A and B are mixed, the filler C added and all three mixed for approx. 3 minutes (5.04 : 1.66 : 23.3 parts by weight, pot life approx. 120 minutes); the mortar is poured in 10–200 mm in one skin (above 200 mm in several skins), flows and compacts itself. No primer is needed on concrete; ≥ 2 N/mm² on concrete from dry to matt damp and on steel; watertight to 5 bar from 10 mm; approx. 65 N/mm² compressive after 24 hours and approx. 109 N/mm² after 7 days.
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/points/0: foot traffic after approx. 12 hours, full resilience after approx. 7 days; Bfl-s1 up to 75 mm
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/points/1: cleaned steel is coated within 4 hours, otherwise primed with {SG3T}
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/points/2: for a slip-resistant mortar surface quartz sand 0.5–1.0 mm is broadcast after approx. 120 minutes, the excess removed and the surface sealed
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/points/3: overcoat min. approx. 12 hours, max. 72 hours without primer
PF_STEPS|/mortarF/points/4: GISCODE RE 30; the safety data sheets are observed
PF_STEPS|/coatThinF/short: {B351} mixed 100 : 24, spread with the trowel in one pass at approx. 1 mm (approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm) and rolled criss-cross with the spiked roller; walkable after 12 hours, full load after 7 days.
